agent.title: Claude Code: migrate atlas-web to sessions v2

messages.content: The auth middleware still reads the old token cookie. Can you move atlas-web over to sessions v2 without logging everyone out?
On it. I will find every place the legacy cookie is read or written first, then migrate in small steps so existing sessions keep working.

Found 14 references in 6 files. Only `session.ts` and `refresh.ts` write the cookie; the rest only read it. Plan:

- Add a `getSession()` helper that reads v2 first, then falls back to the legacy cookie
- Rewrite `middleware.ts` to use it
- Migrate users to v2 silently on their next refresh
- Delete the fallback once the migration window closes
The helper and middleware are done. `useSession` is called in 9 components, so I am leaving its signature alone and changing only what it reads from.
31 of 42 tests pass. The 11 failures are all in `refresh.test.ts`: they stub the old cookie name. I will update the fixtures rather than the code.
Good. Please don't touch the billing routes, they have their own session handling.
Understood, `src/app/billing/**` is off limits. I will keep the change inside `lib`, `hooks` and `middleware`.
Fixtures updated and the refresh tests are green. Running the full suite once more, then I will write up the migration notes.

agent.title: Codex: add retry with backoff to ledger-api uploader
agent.progress: Waiting for approval to run go test

messages.content: The uploader gives up after one failed chunk. Add retry with exponential backoff to ledger-api, and make it configurable.
I will add a small retry wrapper around `uploadChunk` with jitter, capped at five attempts, with the limits set through config.
Only `uploader.go` calls it, so the change is contained. I am adding `UploadRetries` and `UploadBackoffMs` to the config and a `retry.go` helper next to the uploader.
Implemented. The wrapper retries only on network errors and `503`, never on `4xx`, so a bad request still fails fast. Next I want to run the full suite, including the integration tests.
Bash: go test ./... needs your approval

agent.title: OpenCode: split Tide's SettingsView into sections

messages.content: Tide's settings screen has grown a bit wild. Can you split SettingsView into sensible sections and keep behaviour the same?
Yes. I will extract each section into its own view and keep `SettingsView` as a thin list that composes them.
The file is 612 lines with seven natural sections: Reminders, Appearance, Units, Widgets, Sync, Data and About. Settings are shared through a single `SettingsStore`, so the pieces can stay small.
Done. `SettingsView.swift` is now 74 lines, the build is clean, and the previews render all seven sections. Nothing changed in behaviour. Want me to add snapshot tests next?
